messages:
maya: Heads up — I'm prototyping the Console flow for A/B experiments and need a quick sync on two things: default per-variant quotas and how we expose telemetry-driven auto-pause. thinking about UX + the internal API surface. :thinking_face:

samir: for quotas — do you mean rate/throughput quotas or exposure (percentage) caps?

maya: exposure caps. e.g. variant A max 40% of traffic, variant B 10% as a safety cap. but also want per-variant request/sec ceilings for burst safety (so a bad model can't DOS infra).

liam: +1 on both. we currently only have global route qps and experiment-wide splits. adding per-variant token-bucket should be doable but we need to decide precedence: split vs quota when they conflict.

maya: proposal: split defines target allocation, quota is an upper bound that can cut a variant down. routing should normalize remaining traffic among eligible variants. so if variant B hits quota, its assigned share is redistributed proportionally to others.

josh: that sounds reasonable. need to think about deterministic assignment so users get stable variant IDs for session affinity. if we redistribute, must keep bucketing function stable.

olivia: UX note: Console should surface current applied rate vs requested split. show a small "effective allocation" number and a tooltip explaining redistribution. otherwise product teams will be confused when they request 20% but see 5%.

samir: telemetry-driven auto-pause — what triggers? metric regression thresholds, error spikes, latency P95 breach?

maya: yes. product folks want simple toggles: "auto-pause on quality drop" with a linked eval set. Under the hood we can attach policies like: if eval.fail_rate > 5% OR model.latency.p95 > 1.5s for 3m -> mark variant PAUSED and redistribute.

liam: from API perspective we can expose a small policy DSL on experiment config. example prototype:```json
{
  "experiment_id": "exp-2024-06-22-01",
  "variants": [
    {"id":"A","split":0.4,"max_exposure":0.4,"qps_cap":200},
    {"id":"B","split":0.1,"max_exposure":0.1,"qps_cap":50},
    {"id":"C","split":0.5}
  ],
  "auto_pause": [
    {"metric":"eval.fail_rate","op":">","value":0.05,"duration_secs":180},
    {"metric":"model.latency.p95","op":">","value":1.5,"duration_secs":180}
  ]
}
```

maya: looks good. also want an override path for SRE/ops to manually pause/unpause variants and to annotate why.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: experiment-service v3.14.0 to staging at 2024-06-22T14:34:22Z :rocket:

anna: two operational concerns: 1) if many experiments redistribute traffic at once, we might concentrate load on single variant/hardware; need a global smoothener. 2) quota enforcement must be evaluated before model dispatch to avoid wasted compute.

liam: for (1) we can add a global throttle that caps how much redistribution can change a variant's effective allocation per minute. e.g. rate-limit redistribution to +10% per minute. for (2) enforcement path should short-circuit at router: check variant qps token bucket before forwarding to runtime.

josh: API contract question: should the Console send desired "split" or desired "target allocation"? If split is desired, server computes effective allocation after applying caps/guards. keeps UX simpler.

maya: prefer split as primary. Console shows both requested split and effective allocation. also want history graph of effective allocation changes with reasons (quota hit, auto-pause, manual override).

olivia: design will draft a 3-state chip: Requested / Effective / Reason (hover to see timeline). will post mocks by EOD. :sparkles:

samir: telemetry: we need a standard event for allocation changes so dashboards can join it with model-level metrics. event fields: experiment_id, variant_id, requested_split, effective_split, reason, timestamp.

liam: agree. also emit a debug trace id for the routing decision when a request is routed so we can tie a single request to which rule evaluated (for audits). small perf overhead but valuable for debugging.

maya: last bit — rollout API needs a canary ramp helper: console should offer staged ramps (0->1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50%) with automatic checks between steps. if a step fails, stop and optionally rollback. any objections?

josh: make steps configurable and allow "fast-forward" if owner clicks confirm. add a dry-run mode to simulate allocation changes without touching production traffic for testing.

anna: also add backoff logic if infra is overloaded: if global cpu reserved > 85% then pause ramps and alert SRE channel.

maya: great notes. I'll summarize and make a doc with API spec + Console mocks. @samir can you sketch minimal policy DSL impl for the router? @liam can you validate token-bucket perf?

samir: yep will sketch today.

liam: will load test token-bucket path and report numbers by tomorrow.

maya: thanks all :pray: will drop the summary doc in #eng-platform once ready.
